skill.displayName: Pet Adaptive Drying Temperature Recommendation | 宠物烘干温度自适应推荐

version.changelog:
- Enhanced documentation style and structure in SKILL.md for better readability and usability, including visual modules, scenario overviews, and formatted step-by-step guides.
- Clarified workflow, trigger rules, and strict cloud API requirements for historical report queries.
- Expanded presentation of parameters, resource links, and standardized output/report formatting.
- Removed redundant or duplicate documentation (skill-card.md).
- No code logic changes; updates are entirely focused on improved skill description and usage instructions.

llm.summary: The skill’s pet-analysis function is real and mostly disclosed, but it silently creates or reuses an identity, logs in to a remote service, and stores auth tokens locally.

dimensions.detail: Remote pet image/video analysis, history lookup, and report export are described in the skill, but automatic account/identity handling and token persistence materially exceed what a user would expect from a drying-temperature recommender.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs automatic cloud history queries and internal identity use without asking the user; hidden command-line identity/API-key parameters are suppressed from help, which reduces user visibility.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution or destructive setup was found. A dev config contains raw private-IP service URLs, but the packaged default config selects production endpoints, so this is not enough by itself to hold the skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Reading local media for upload is purpose-aligned and disclosed, but the shared utility also probes workspace layout, creates shared data directories, and reads data/smyx-api-key.txt as an identity source.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill can create a local SQLite database, create/reuse default users, call a remote phone-login/registration endpoint, and cache token/open_token values locally; this is high-impact persistence for the stated use case.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. This skill will send pet media or URLs to remote services and may query cloud history. More importantly, it can silently create or reuse an internal user identity, read a local smyx-api-key.txt value, register/login with a remote service, and store returned tokens in a local SQLite database. Install only if you are comfortable with that account and credential handling, and avoid using sensitive household media unless you trust the service and its retention practices.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: Shell/script use and remote API calls are disclosed, but the artifact does not clearly disclose the full identity, credential, and local persistence model.
[SDI-2] expected: Cloud history lookup is explicitly documented as a trigger and workflow, so the history feature itself is not hidden; the associated automatic identity handling remains a concern.
[SDI-1] expected: History pagination and report export endpoints match the documented report-list/report-link behavior.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The --list path is documented, but the suppressed open-id parameter and silent identity resolution make the access boundary under-disclosed.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Generic CRUD/raw HTTP helpers are broader than this specific pet-analysis workflow, though the main user path calls fixed backend endpoints.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The arbitrary HTTP wrapper is overbroad for the declared feature, but I did not find evidence that the normal workflow accepts arbitrary destinations beyond user media URLs and configured API routes.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Local user-account persistence is only partially explained as internal identity handling and is not proportionate without clearer disclosure.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Storing token and open_token fields in the local SQLite user table is a material credential-exposure concern.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The default trigger can activate on ordinary pet media needing analysis, which may be broader than explicit drying-temperature intent.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading local files or sending URLs to a remote analysis API is expected for this cloud-analysis skill and is stated in the description, but retention and privacy details are thin.
[E1] unexpected: The phone-login/registration POST sends user-linked identifiers to a remote service and is not clearly disclosed as part of the pet-analysis workflow.
[P2] expected: The reported hidden character appears to be a zero-width joiner used in an emoji sequence in a visible table row, not an artifact-backed hidden instruction.
[YR4] expected: The manifest description is long and bilingual but describes the same pet-analysis workflow; I did not find separate metadata-poisoning instructions.
[static:suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: The raw-IP URLs are present only in a dev config while the default config uses production lifeemergence.com/open.lifeemergence.com endpoints, so this was downgraded.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry is clean and does not add a negative signal.
